review.notes: Targeting is unchanged: `e1:SetProperty(EFFECT_FLAG_CARD_TARGET)` is present in BOTH scripts and both call `Duel.SelectTarget`, so the lineage's "Select 1 ..." (v0-v2) -> "Target 1 ..." (v3, LCYW-EN145, 2012-09-29) is cosmetic per the explicit test in the review instructions. The "face-up" (added v2, SDMM-EN026, 2010-02-19) and "you control" clauses were already enforced by both scripts via `c:IsFaceup()` and the LOCATION_MZONE/controller check, and the resolution-time `tc:IsRelateToEffect(e) and tc:IsFaceup()` guard plus the CARD_BLUEEYES_SPIRIT clamp are identical in both. Whole text lineage v0 (RDS-EN041, 2004-12-01) through v5 (OP08-EN008, 2018-08-17) therefore recorded as cosmetic, hence modern_text_version null. Verification-half bounds: old attested through 2011-02-02, modern from 2019-04-03.

event.historical_text: Select 1 Machine-Type monster with an ATK of 500 or less on your side of the field and activate this card. You can Special Summon up to 2 cards with the same name from your Deck.
event.summary: Period ruling package. Activation condition: the modern `s.filter` requires, on top of face-up/Machine/500-or-less-ATK, that `Duel.IsExistingMatchingCard(s.filter2,tp,LOCATION_DECK,0,1,nil,c:GetCode(),e,tp)` - a Deck copy of the chosen monster's name - while the goat filter drops that clause, so the card can be activated targeting a Machine whose copies are all gone. Failed-search verification: the goat operation adds `else Duel.GoatConfirm(tp,LOCATION_DECK)`. Only the verification half is dated by the shared search-verification chronology, so the change is recorded unresolved.
